methodology.how: _provenance.write_manifest (:49) serialises a fixed v1 record -- schema_version, source_kind, source_vintage, built_at, node_count, edge_count -- to a path derived from the database path by manifest_path() (:44), which appends MANIFEST_SUFFIX '._build_manifest.json' (:34). It is written by each Kuzu loader on a SUCCESSFUL build, so the manifest's existence is itself a claim that a build completed. The three members correspond 1:1 to three build mechanisms, and each records a source_vintage shaped for its own mechanism: 'nessie' carries Iceberg metadata keys and snapshot ids, 'tarball' carries a bucket and tarball key, 'stitch' carries a source path and mtime.

declared_opinions: THE MANIFEST IS A SIBLING, NOT A CHILD (:21-23). Placed at <db_path>._build_manifest.json rather than inside the DB, explicitly so it survives whether Kuzu materialises the DB as a file or a directory, AND so a --force wipe of the DB never clobbers the about-to-be-rewritten manifest. A deliberate placement with two stated reasons.

PROVENANCE GOES TO STDERR, NEVER STDOUT (:24-25). So comp-kuzu --json and table output stay machine-parseable while provenance is still always surfaced. A declared position about not making the caller choose between clean output and knowing the vintage.
AN ABSENT MANIFEST MUST BE LOUD, NEVER SILENT (:26). The module states this as a design commitment (F1), and unusually for a claim of this kind it is honoured in code -- see failure_mode.

key.identity_space: The DATABASE PATH. A manifest has no identifier of its own -- its identity is entirely derived from the DB it sits beside, via manifest_path(db_path) = db_path + '._build_manifest.json' (:44, :34).
key.key_expression: `manifest_path(db_path) = db_path.rstrip('/\\') + MANIFEST_SUFFIX`, where MANIFEST_SUFFIX is the module-level constant `'._build_manifest.json'` (infra/aws/globgrph/_provenance.py:34, function at :44). A manifest carries NO identifier of its own: given the DB path the manifest path is pure string concatenation, and the INVERSE -- stripping the suffix -- recovers the DB path a manifest belongs to, which is why this row's identity_space is the DATABASE path rather than the manifest's. ⚠ The `rstrip('/\\')` is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a DB given as a DIRECTORY with a trailing separator would otherwise produce a manifest path with the separator embedded, and the inverse would not recover the DB path.
key.declared_mapping: manifest_path(db_path) -> f'{db_path}{MANIFEST_SUFFIX}' (:44 with the suffix constant at :34). That expression is the whole mapping between the database-path space and the manifest-path space.
key.evidence:
key_is_stable='stable' measured by construction and by observation: the suffix is a module-level constant, the transform is pure string concatenation, and all three declared paths resolve to real files, so no member carries a name that fails to bind. crosses_spaces=TRUE and measured -- a DB path is not a manifest path until the suffix is appended, and the two spaces are distinct even though one is a prefix of the other. ⛔ THE DERIVED IDENTITY IS THE FAMILY'S CENTRAL STRENGTH AND ITS CENTRAL FRAGILITY, AND BOTH FOLLOW FROM THE SAME LINE. Strength: a manifest can never be orphaned from its DB by a rename of the manifest, because nothing references the manifest by name -- the reader always reconstructs the path from the DB it was asked about. Fragility: RENAME OR MOVE THE DATABASE AND THE MANIFEST SILENTLY STOPS BEING FOUND. It is not deleted and it is not stale; it simply no longer sits at the derived path, and the reader reports UNKNOWN VINTAGE for a database whose provenance is intact one filename away. Nothing in the module detects that case, because from the reader's side it is byte-identical to a build that never wrote a manifest. || v3 delta pass: key_expression ABSENT on this card (not yet declared by the carding lane); row basis lowered from measured to the floor.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: ⛔ LOUD, AND THIS IS THE FAMILY'S BEST PROPERTY -- rare enough on this wave that I verified it in code rather than accepting the docstring. read_manifest (:74) returns None when the manifest is absent or unparseable, and the header renderer does NOT silently omit the section: at :575 it calls read_manifest and at :578, on None, appends the literal '!! UNKNOWN VINTAGE -- no _build_manifest.json beside this DB.' to the provenance header that comp-kuzu prints on EVERY invocation. So a missing manifest surfaces to the caller as an explicit banner, not as absence.
silent_degrade_paths: A RENAMED OR MOVED DATABASE takes its manifest out of the derived path. The reader then prints UNKNOWN VINTAGE -- loud, but WRONG about the cause: the provenance exists and is intact, it is simply no longer where the rule looks. Loud about the symptom, silent about the reason.

node_count and edge_count are build-time assertions that nothing re-derives. A DB modified after its build carries a manifest whose counts are confidently stale, and no mechanism compares them to reality.

verdict.why: This is the healthiest family I have carded across two waves, and its central property is one almost nothing else on this estate has: IT FAILS LOUD. An absent manifest does not degrade to silence -- comp-kuzu prints an explicit UNKNOWN VINTAGE banner on every invocation, and I verified that in the implementation at :575-578 rather than accepting the docstring's claim at :26, because this same session produced two instances of a module describing itself incorrectly. It is the only card in my set carrying distinguishable_from_true_negative='yes'. The family is 3 of 3 present with 0 undeclared, its members map 1:1 onto three distinct source_kinds, its identity is derived from the DB path so a manifest cannot be orphaned by its own rename, and its sibling placement is documented with two reasons. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on four measured defects: (1) all three members are UNTRACKED and not gitignored, so the clean 3-of-3 is a fact about THIS DEVICE and no repository-plane instrument can observe the family at all -- the same property that made my third subject's enumeration disjoint from reality, where this family's correctness is luck rather than method; (2) one member's recorded vintage is already superseded -- kuzu_nessie_db records nodes_snapshot 2902399899597701830 while live is 1462710383782792396 -- and nothing anywhere compares the two, so the divergence surfaces only to a reader who fetches both planes; (3) the derived identity means a MOVED database produces a loud UNKNOWN VINTAGE that is right about the symptom and wrong about the cause, indistinguishable from a build that never wrote provenance; (4) source_vintage is polymorphic across three incompatible shapes with no declared discriminator beyond source_kind, and one member's vintage is a device-absolute path that resolves on exactly one machine. Not UNSOUND: every member is present, parseable, internally consistent, and honest about what it recorded. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows worked, every scalar measured. ⛔ NO COMPLETENESS CLAIM ACROSS THE ESTATE -- the untracked members make that unmeasurable, and I say so rather than reporting a device count as an estate count. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane rebuilt nothing, ran no loader, and committed nothing to _provenance.py or to any Kuzu database.
